title: How to create good habits
paragraphs: Have you ever made a promise to yourself that you didn’t keep? Commonly, when the new year ticks over, we make resolutions: going to the gym, studying harder or giving up a bad habit. Sadly, not long after we’ve made the promise, we often end up breaking them. But what if you want to create a new good habit? Well, it’s possible, but willpower might not be the only thing you need.

The basic idea of a habit is something we do almost unconsciously, as if you’re on autopilot. An example of this would be having breakfast or saying ‘please’ and ‘thank you’. Good habits can be part of your daily routine. But if we don’t have those habits, how can we create them? According to a study published by the European Journal of Social Psychology, it takes an average of 66 days to form a new habit. However, relying only on determination may not be the answer.

Questioning why you want something to be the norm rather than relying on your resolve could be the key. Do you want to lose weight because you want to be healthier or feel more attractive? The issue is, willpower could be subject to your mood – a bad mood may mean you don’t want to do something.

You should also avoid trying to change too much at once – remember that it’s a case of baby steps. Giving up all your favourite foods, going to the gym, and stopping drinking at the same time will probably result in failure rather than sustainable practice. And don’t worry about failing – just start again!

Finally, don’t do things outside your comfort zone. If you hate mushrooms, don’t persevere and try to add them to your diet just to be healthier. Eat something you like! It might not be quick, but if you follow these tips, you may be able to change something for the better or kick a bad habit.

vocabulary.entry: resolution /ˌrezəˈluːʃn/ n. （新年等的）决心
vocabulary.example: She made a resolution to read one book every month.
vocabulary.translation: 她下定决心每个月读一本书。

vocabulary.entry: willpower /ˈwɪlpaʊə/ n. 意志力
vocabulary.example: It takes a lot of willpower to give up smoking.
vocabulary.translation: 戒烟需要很强的意志力。

vocabulary.entry: unconsciously /ʌnˈkɒnʃəsli/ adv. 无意识地；不知不觉地
vocabulary.example: He unconsciously tapped his foot to the rhythm of the music.
vocabulary.translation: 他不知不觉地跟着音乐的节奏轻敲脚尖。

vocabulary.entry: autopilot /ˈɔːtəpaɪlət/ n. 自动驾驶模式
vocabulary.example: She drove to work on autopilot, thinking about the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 她开着车几乎是自动驾驶，脑子里想着会议的事。

vocabulary.entry: daily routine /ˈdeɪli ruːˈtiːn/ n. 日常惯例；日常作息
vocabulary.example: Yoga has become part of my daily routine.
vocabulary.translation: 瑜伽已经成为我日常作息的一部分。

vocabulary.entry: publish /ˈpʌblɪʃ/ v. 发表；出版
vocabulary.example: The research team plans to publish their findings next month.
vocabulary.translation: 这个研究团队计划下个月发表他们的研究成果。

vocabulary.entry: determination /dɪˌtɜːmɪˈneɪʃn/ n. 决心；坚定
vocabulary.example: Her determination helped her overcome many difficulties.
vocabulary.translation: 她的坚定帮她克服了许多困难。

vocabulary.entry: norm /nɔːm/ n. 常态；常规
vocabulary.example: Working from home has become the new norm in many companies.
vocabulary.translation: 居家办公已经成为许多公司的新常态。

vocabulary.entry: resolve /rɪˈzɒlv/ n. 决心；决意
vocabulary.example: She kept her resolve to run a marathon despite the injury.
vocabulary.translation: 尽管受了伤，她还是坚持要跑马拉松的决心。

vocabulary.entry: be subject to /bi ˈsʌbdʒɪkt tuː/ 受……影响；取决于
vocabulary.example: The plan is subject to the manager's approval.
vocabulary.translation: 这项计划需经经理批准。

vocabulary.entry: at once /æt wʌns/ adv. 同时；立刻
vocabulary.example: Don't try to do everything at once; take it step by step.
vocabulary.translation: 不要试图同时做所有事，要一步一步来。

vocabulary.entry: baby step /ˈbeɪbi step/ n. 一小步；循序渐进的步骤
vocabulary.example: Learning a new language requires baby steps, starting with basic vocabulary.
vocabulary.translation: 学习一门新语言需要循序渐进，从基础词汇开始。

vocabulary.entry: result in /rɪˈzʌlt ɪn/ 导致；造成
vocabulary.example: Careless driving can result in serious accidents.
vocabulary.translation: 粗心驾驶可能会导致严重的事故。

vocabulary.entry: sustainable /səˈsteɪnəbl/ adj. 可持续的；能长期坚持的
vocabulary.example: We need to find a sustainable solution to the environmental problem.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要找到一个解决环境问题的可持续方案。

vocabulary.entry: practice /ˈpræktɪs/ n. 习惯做法；惯例
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise is a good practice for staying healthy.
vocabulary.translation: 规律锻炼是保持健康的好习惯。

vocabulary.entry: comfort zone /ˈkʌmfət zəʊn/ n. 舒适区
vocabulary.example: It's important to step out of your comfort zone to grow.
vocabulary.translation: 走出舒适区对个人成长很重要。

vocabulary.entry: persevere /ˌpɜːsəˈvɪə/ v. 坚持；执意
vocabulary.example: She persevered with her studies even when she felt tired.
vocabulary.translation: 即使感到疲惫，她还是坚持学习。

vocabulary.entry: diet /ˈdaɪət/ n. 日常饮食；膳食
vocabulary.example: A balanced diet is essential for good health.
vocabulary.translation: 均衡的饮食对健康至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: tip /tɪp/ n. 建议；实用的小窍门
vocabulary.example: Here are some tips for improving your writing skills.
vocabulary.translation: 这里有一些提升写作技巧的建议。

vocabulary.entry: kick /kɪk/ v. 戒掉（坏习惯）
vocabulary.example: He finally kicked his habit of staying up late.
vocabulary.translation: 他终于戒掉了熬夜的坏习惯。

vocabulary.entry: break /breɪk/ v. 违背（承诺）；打破
vocabulary.example: He broke his promise to help me with the project.
vocabulary.translation: 他违背了帮我做这个项目的承诺。

vocabulary.entry: form /fɔːm/ v. 养成（习惯）；形成
vocabulary.example: It's easier to form a good habit when you're young.
vocabulary.translation: 年轻时更容易养成好习惯。

vocabulary.entry: rely on /rɪˈlaɪ ɒn/ 依赖；依靠
vocabulary.example: You can't rely on others to solve your problems for you.
vocabulary.translation: 你不能依赖别人帮你解决问题。

vocabulary.entry: attractive /əˈtræktɪv/ adj. 有吸引力的；好看的
vocabulary.example: The hotel is in an attractive location near the beach.
vocabulary.translation: 这家酒店位置很好，就在海滩附近。

vocabulary.entry: mood /muːd/ n. 心情；情绪
vocabulary.example: Listening to music can help improve your mood.
vocabulary.translation: 听音乐有助于改善心情。

sentences.english: Have you ever made a promise to yourself that you didn’t keep?
sentences.chinese: 你是否曾对自己许下承诺，最后却没能遵守？

sentences.english: Commonly, when the new year ticks over, we make resolutions: going to the gym, studying harder or giving up a bad habit.
sentences.chinese: 通常，每当新年钟声敲响，我们都会立下新年决心：去健身房锻炼、更努力学习或是戒掉某个坏习惯。

sentences.english: Sadly, not long after we’ve made the promise, we often end up breaking them.
sentences.chinese: 遗憾的是，许下诺言后没过多久，我们往往就会违背它。

sentences.english: But what if you want to create a new good habit?
sentences.chinese: 但如果你想养成一个新的好习惯呢？

sentences.english: Well, it’s possible, but willpower might not be the only thing you need.
sentences.chinese: 这并非不可能，但意志力或许并非你唯一需要的东西。

sentences.english: The basic idea of a habit is something we do almost unconsciously, as if you’re on autopilot.
sentences.chinese: 习惯的本质，是我们近乎无意识、如同自动驾驶般做出的行为。

sentences.english: An example of this would be having breakfast or saying ‘please’ and ‘thank you’.
sentences.chinese: 比如吃早餐、说“请”和“谢谢”，这些都是习惯。

sentences.english: Good habits can be part of your daily routine.
sentences.chinese: 好习惯可以成为日常生活的一部分。

sentences.english: But if we don’t have those habits, how can we create them?
sentences.chinese: 但如果我们本身没有这些习惯，该如何养成呢？

sentences.english: According to a study published by the European Journal of Social Psychology, it takes an average of 66 days to form a new habit.
sentences.chinese: 根据《欧洲社会心理学杂志》发表的一项研究，养成一个新习惯平均需要66天。

sentences.english: However, relying only on determination may not be the answer.
sentences.chinese: 不过，只靠决心可能并不够。

sentences.english: Questioning why you want something to be the norm rather than relying on your resolve could be the key.
sentences.chinese: 关键或许在于，问自己为何想让某件事成为常态，而非单纯依赖决心。

sentences.english: Do you want to lose weight because you want to be healthier or feel more attractive?
sentences.chinese: 你想要减肥，是为了更健康，还是为了让自己看起来更有魅力？

sentences.english: The issue is, willpower could be subject to your mood – a bad mood may mean you don’t want to do something.
sentences.chinese: 问题的关键是，意志力会受情绪影响——心情不好的时候，你可能就不想去做既定的事了。

sentences.english: You should also avoid trying to change too much at once – remember that it’s a case of baby steps.
sentences.chinese: 你还应该避免试图一蹴而就——要记住，凡事都要循序渐进。

sentences.english: Giving up all your favourite foods, going to the gym, and stopping drinking at the same time will probably result in failure rather than sustainable practice.
sentences.chinese: 一下子戒掉所有爱吃的食物、坚持去健身房锻炼、同时还戒酒，这样做很可能会失败，而非形成可持续的习惯。

sentences.english: And don’t worry about failing – just start again!
sentences.chinese: 而且别害怕失败——大不了重新开始！

sentences.english: Finally, don’t do things outside your comfort zone.
sentences.chinese: 最后，不要做超出自己舒适区的事。

sentences.english: If you hate mushrooms, don’t persevere and try to add them to your diet just to be healthier.
sentences.chinese: 如果你讨厌蘑菇，就不要为了健康而勉强自己吃。

sentences.english: Eat something you like!
sentences.chinese: 吃一些自己喜欢的食物就好！

sentences.english: It might not be quick, but if you follow these tips, you may be able to change something for the better or kick a bad habit.
sentences.chinese: 这个过程或许不会一蹴而就，但只要遵循这些建议，你或许就能做出积极的改变，或是戒掉某个坏习惯。
